ideas.children_he: יוֹסֵף פָּגַשׁ בְּבֵית הַסֹּהַר שְׁנֵי שָׂרִים שֶׁל פַּרְעֹה.
ideas.children_en: The chief cupbearer and baker sinned against the king and were put in prison, where Joseph served them with special care because of their status.

ideas.children_he: יוֹסֵף שָׂם לֵב שֶׁהַשָּׂרִים עֲצוּבִים וְשָׁאַל מַדּוּעַ.
ideas.children_en: The officers had confusing dreams, and Joseph asked why they looked upset. He wanted them to tell their dreams to help understand them.

ideas.children_he: יוֹסֵף הִסְבִּיר לְשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים אֶת חֲלוֹמוֹ וּבִקֵּשׁ שֶׁיִּזְכֹּר אוֹתוֹ.
ideas.children_en: The cupbearer told of a dream with a grapevine, and Joseph said it means he will be restored in three days. Joseph asked him to remember him after he is free.

ideas.children_he: לִפְעָמִים בְּשׂוֹרָה אֵינָהּ נְעִימָה, אֲבָל חָשׁוּב לוֹמַר אֶת הָאֱמֶת.
ideas.children_en: The baker dreamed of three baskets on his head eaten by birds, which Joseph said means he will die in three days and be eaten by birds.
On Pharaoh’s birthday, he restored the cupbearer but hanged the baker, just as Joseph predicted in their dreams.

ideas.children_he: שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים שָׁכַח אֶת יוֹסֵף. כְּשֶׁמִּישֶׁהוּ עוֹזֵר לָנוּ, חָשׁוּב לִזְכֹּר אוֹתוֹ.
ideas.children_en: The cupbearer saw Joseph’s dream come true but forgot to mention him to Pharaoh because he never met Joseph again.
